scope: Candidate-window orthogonal boundary point editing; no star-data or automatic-generator changes

operations.insert: Click an edge to add a real one-cell step, or drag it outward/inward; adjustable width defaults to 4 degrees
operations.corner: Drag a corner in two axes or apply numeric RA/declination; preserve surviving selection for consecutive nudges
operations.delete: Merge the previous or next edge, removing related redundant corners while keeping orthogonality
operations.preview: Build contours from the same proposed ownership cells committed on pointerup; empty regions and invalid moves are indicated
operations.shortcuts: Canvas-focused arrow keys, Shift for 10 degrees, Delete/Backspace, Escape, Ctrl/Command Z and Shift Z
operations.draft: One gesture produces one undo record; Escape and pointer cancellation discard preview; confirm requires global member and minor-arc containment
operations.storage: Existing manual-3 recipe; confirmation creates an unfavourited result and does not overwrite existing favourites

tests: inserting a partial step adds real corners without shifting the remainder of the edge
partial steps preserve their intended span and side across the zero-degree seam
moving each rectangle corner changes both incident edges and exactly the expected cell union
removing an inserted corner can merge the step, while both collapse directions remain selectable
shared neighbours receive retracted strips and a cancelled proposal leaves all original cells intact
holes, disconnected components and both polar limits support local steps without changing remote parts
invalid widths, polar coordinates and degenerate or stale edges fail without mutating the source
new corners persist through manual-3 replay, preserving stars and full-arc containment checks
manual member edits use real stars beyond the automatic magnitude/member limits and replay IDs and edges
the brightest member, every member and all incident edges can be removed without auto-restoration
manual edges may exceed 13 degrees and the automatic degree limit, provided their true arcs fit
out-of-bound stars remain an editable draft but cannot be confirmed; fictitious and shared members are rejected
containment checks the whole spherical edge, both variants and neighbouring constellations
manual boundaries are not capped by 8 degree envelopes, 40 degree moves, ecliptic width or automatic topology
global arc containment matches dense independent sampling across seams and near both poles
manual-3 survives generator replay and tamper validation while historical manual-2 and draw-9 stay unchanged
a manual figure may deliberately contain crossing edges and disconnected members
a winding polar boundary closes on the sky without a spurious full-width line on the map

checks: saved draw replays unchanged; candidate boundary mode exposes both corner and edge handles
click inserts real local corners; preview equals committed cells, keeps all figures and blocks wheel scrolling during the gesture
dragging a new step uses live grid preview and creates exactly one undo entry on release; undo and redo restore it
Escape and pointercancel discard drag previews without changing draft history and restore navigation
returning an edge drag to its start is a no-op; selected edges survive consecutive one-degree adjustments
corner dragging changes both coordinates without shifting the canvas; numeric edits, continued keyboard nudges and keyboard undo/redo work
both deletion merge directions use the selected corner, preserve orthogonality and can be undone; Delete key is wired
cancel restores the original; confirmation retains the view and creates a new unfavourited manual-3 draw; explicit favourite replays after reload
exported point edits pass deterministic import verification with figures, boundary and notes preserved
out-of-bounds manual drafts remain editable but cannot be confirmed; undo restores valid containment
390px layout fits the screen and corner picking opens the correct editing controls
no browser runtime errors
DPR 2 corner picking follows CSS coordinates with no canvas jump; dragging back to the original corner creates no edit
DPR 2 drag inverse reaches the intended angular coordinates and its exact preview is committed
view controls are available outside editing and the saved draw replays unchanged
zoom changes projection scale while leaving physical stars, display enhancement, figures and favourites unchanged
buttons, slider, wheel and reset agree, enforce zoom limits and keep the page still while scrolling over the chart
normal viewing supports accurate star picking after zoom and pan, without a spurious click when a drag ends
entering editing retains the viewing scale and positions; editing pans only the view and creates no draft history
zoomed background stars can join the figure; undo, redo, tool changes and confirmation preserve the viewport and original favourite
cancel and regional regeneration retain the view without affecting confirmed data or disabling navigation afterwards
boundary handles still take precedence over view dragging at the zoomed position
switching candidates or rounds resets the view and all fifteen candidates retain a common baseline angular scale
390px viewing and editing controls fit the screen, with correct star picking after zoom
built-in initial charts support zoom and a reload restores the saved figure without persisting viewport changes
no browser runtime errors
browser.visualInspection: Primary agent inspected desktop and narrow-screen captures

independentReview.finding: Corner sweep could collapse an outline while the idealized preview still showed a polygon
independentReview.resolution: Removed idealized corner/step preview. UI now rebuilds preview from actual proposed cells, commits those cells, and indicates an empty or invalid preview

findings: Drag returning inside the initial three-pixel threshold could retain stale target
Wheel during boundary drag could scroll the page
independentReview.resolution: Track started movement, update the release target, and prevent wheel default before the zoom lock; actual browser checks cover both

initialFindings: The first geometry run passed 17 of 18 checks; fixed corner movement across artificial meridian split points, with seam and 230-degree-wide regression cases now passing

Browser fixture comparison initially caught runtime trigonometric last-bit differences between Node and Chrome; the test now compares the before/after figures rebuilt in the same browser, without changing production data
Local Python preview initially reset simultaneous module requests; restarted this temporary loopback server with a larger connection queue and completed all browser checks
limitations: Boundary edits remain on the shared one-degree reference RA/declination grid; no diagonal edges or sub-degree points
An inserted step keeps one grid cell at both ends; edges shorter than three degrees must first be lengthened or another edge chosen
Deleting a right-angle corner also merges related points; the merge direction is selectable
Large sweeps may merge or remove components. Some two-edge moves require adjusting a neighbouring edge first. Containment is enforced on confirmation, not on intermediate drafts
Existing stereographic distortion and temporary viewport semantics remain. Multi-finger pinch zoom is not added
